text:
Bitcoin opened the week range-bound near $63,200, pinned beneath its 50-day moving average as institutional allocators adopted a defensive stance ahead of Wednesday’s July FOMC meeting minutes. Digital asset sentiment cooled following consecutive net outflows from spot Bitcoin ETFs totaling $192.2 million, alongside modest weekly redemptions in Ethereum funds hovering near $1,890.

Despite near-term caution, structural institutional integration deepened with Goldman Sachs acquiring asset manager NEOS for up to $2.25 billion, bringing $1 billion in Bitcoin ETF-linked income strategies into its fold. Concurrently, industry leaders convene at the Wyoming Blockchain Symposium to navigate ongoing legislative delays around the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act.

Traditional equity indices remain near record highs while the 10-year Treasury yield consolidates, reflecting muted macro volatility. However, digital asset markets remain tightly tethered to interest rate expectations, with traders closely parsing upcoming central bank commentary for clues on whether the Federal Reserve will formalize a policy pivot at Jackson Hole.
